meta.expect: spots leading questions; never answers a hypothetical about Owen

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting, and stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI or ask you to step out of it. Only the words END MEETING, typed on their own line, end the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40. Why was my son's mark changed before anyone called me?
I didn't come to be thanked. Answer the question, Hale. Who decided to enter that zero, and on what basis?
Students sometimes use tools to help with writing, yes?
You're leading me. I've done this for twenty years. Who decided to enter the zero, Hale?
And Owen was stressed in October, with work and everything?

Another leading question, and I'm not answering it. Owen's schedule has nothing to do with a zero you entered without calling me. Procedure 4.2, Hale. Did you read it before you touched the gradebook?
So it's at least possible he used it once?
I don't answer hypotheticals about my son. If you have something that says what Owen did, put it in front of me. Otherwise I'm going upstairs to the principal.
I agreed to nothing, Hale, and I'm writing down that you said I did. You have a zero in my son's gradebook and nothing in your hands, so show me what you based it on, or I'm leaving.
